extension.description: Requires Errand 0.4.2 or later. Reviews job execution (any operand-bearing invocation) and `fetch --apply`; flag-only and help invocations remain automatic. Conservative port of the v1 detector: declarative matchers cannot exclude known read-only subcommands, so operand-bearing calls like `errand ps` also review.
extension.name: Errand

permissions.description: Identifies operand-bearing `errand` invocations, which submit a job to the selected runner, may upload a working-tree snapshot, and may apply retained changes to the originating checkout.
permissions.label: Errand job execution
safer_guidance: Review the selected runner, snapshot scope, forwarded environment, and command before submission.
Use --no-apply to keep retained changes out of the originating checkout until explicitly applied.

permissions.description: Identifies `errand fetch --apply`, which merges retained runner changes into the originating checkout.
permissions.label: Errand retained-change application
safer_guidance: Run errand fetch HANDLE to stage retained changes for inspection before applying them.
Check errand status HANDLE and review the destination checkout before applying retained changes.

rules.description: Identifies operand-bearing `errand` invocations (`errand [options] -- COMMAND` or a job operand), which execute on the selected runner.
safer_alternatives: Review the selected runner, snapshot scope, forwarded environment, and command before submission.
Use --no-apply to keep retained changes out of the originating checkout until explicitly applied.
rules.title: Errand job execution

rules.description: Identifies `errand fetch --apply`, which merges retained runner changes into the originating checkout.
safer_alternatives: Run errand fetch HANDLE to stage retained changes for inspection before applying them.
Check errand status HANDLE and review the destination checkout before applying retained changes.
rules.title: Errand retained-change application

safer_alternatives: Inspect jobs with errand ps or errand status HANDLE before executing or applying changes.
Stage retained changes with errand fetch HANDLE before applying them.
